quickStations.title: Anchors and scales
quickStations.question: How do physicists agree on a second, metre, and quantum of action in the International System of Units (SI)?
quickStations.interaction: Inspect fixed defining anchors, then test dimensions and quantity kinds in the workshop.

quickStations.title: Unit bridges
quickStations.question: How can a photon energy be mapped to frequency and vacuum wavelength, then to derived equivalent mass and temperature scales?
quickStations.interaction: Convert one photon energy across labeled representations without assigning photon rest mass or a thermal state.

quickStations.title: Electrical standards
quickStations.question: How do fixed h and e support quantum electrical reference relationships and their practical realizations?
quickStations.interaction: Trace exact SI relationships, practical devices, and historical conventional values without conflating them.

quickStations.title: Atoms and materials
quickStations.question: How can calibrated spectra constrain a model of atomic structure?
quickStations.interaction: Relate wavelength, frequency, and transition energy under a hydrogen-like model, while treating selection rules as context that this engine does not evaluate.

quickStations.title: Particles and mass
quickStations.question: How are massive-particle rest energy, momentum, and quantum wavelengths related without treating them as independent measurements?
quickStations.interaction: Compare electron and proton rest energies and Compton scales, then keep de Broglie wavelength tied to momentum.

quickStations.title: Spin and magnetism
quickStations.question: How does a stated spin-moment model predict magnetic response in an applied field?
quickStations.interaction: Predict and calculate precession frequency, then distinguish the model output from a measurement.

quickStations.title: Heat and radiation
quickStations.question: How do thermal models connect temperature, microscopic energy scales, and radiation?
quickStations.interaction: Change modeled temperature and calculate a black-body spectrum.

quickStations.title: Molar matter
quickStations.question: How do particle-scale quantities become laboratory matter?
quickStations.interaction: Scale particles into moles, gas volumes, and bulk quantities.

chapters.title: Reproduction Is Not Validation
chapters.question: What does it mean when software reproduces a number?
chapters.summary: Distinguish definitions, identities, measurements, calibrations, predictions, reproductions, comparisons, validations, and blind tests. A successful computation shows that an implementation ran under recorded inputs; it does not by itself validate the associated physical theory.

caveats: A chapter shell defines curriculum scope; it is not an evaluated scientific result.

chapters.title: Units, Dimensions, and Physical Quantities
chapters.question: Why can a numerically correct expression still be physically meaningless?
chapters.summary: Build physical quantities from dimensions and unit coordinates, then change units without changing the represented physics. Dimensional consistency is necessary for a physical equation, but it does not establish that the equation is empirically correct.

chapters.title: Measurement, Uncertainty, and Standards
chapters.question: How precise is a physical number?
chapters.summary: Separate defined values from measured values and interpret significant digits, standard uncertainty, covariance, conventions, and standard states. Exact definitions and algebraic identities are not observations and receive no z-score; a z-score applies only to a declared comparison of uncertain values with covariance and dependence handled.

caveats: A chapter shell defines curriculum scope; it is not an evaluated statistical comparison.

chapters.title: Anatomy of a Formula Recipe
chapters.question: Where does the expected result enter the calculation?
chapters.summary: Trace scale factors, conversions, dimensionless terms, root corrections, dependency passes, and target-aware expression selection in formula recipes. Algebraic complexity does not establish independence when a target scale is already embedded in an input or selected factor.

caveats: A chapter shell defines curriculum scope; it does not report a completed formula audit.

chapters.title: Clocks, Action, Light, and Gravity
chapters.question: How do reproducible standards anchor scales from the laboratory to the Planck regime?
chapters.summary: Connect the caesium-133 frequency, speed of light, Planck constants, Newtonian gravity, luminous efficacy, and Planck scales. Derived units and normalized coordinates expose relationships among standards, identities, and models without turning reference choices into new predictions.

caveats: A chapter shell defines curriculum scope; it is not an evaluated scientific result.

chapters.title: Frequency, Energy, Mass, and Temperature
chapters.question: How can photon energy map to frequency and vacuum wavelength, then to derived equivalent mass and temperature scales?
chapters.summary: Use E_gamma = h nu and nu = c/lambda for a photon propagating in vacuum, then derive the labeled scales E_gamma/c^2 and E_gamma/k_B. These representations do not assign photon rest mass or assert a thermal system at the equivalent temperature, and massive-particle rest energy remains a separate relationship.

caveats: Equivalent scales are derived labels, not independent observations or physical-state assignments.

chapters.title: Charge and Quantum Electrical Standards
chapters.question: How do fixed h and e support exact quantum electrical relationships and their practical realizations?
chapters.summary: Trace fixed elementary charge and Planck's constant through exact ideal conductance, resistance, Josephson, and magnetic-flux relationships while keeping practical device realization, corrections, and uncertainty separate from pre-2019 conventional values. Vacuum permeability and permittivity are not independently fixed exact standards in the present SI.

caveats: Exact ideal relationships do not make practical realizations uncertainty-free.

chapters.title: Atomic Structure and Spectroscopy
chapters.question: How can a calibrated spectrum constrain an atomic-structure model?
chapters.summary: Relate hydrogen-like energy levels and transitions to wavelength and frequency under a stated Hamiltonian. Line identification, calibration, selection rules, broadening assumptions, reduced mass, and competing-model checks constrain inference; a spectrum does not reveal a unique atomic structure by inspection, and dimensional combinations cannot replace a bound-state model.

caveats: Spectral inference is model- and calibration-dependent.

chapters.title: Particle Mass and Quantum Wavelength
chapters.question: How are invariant mass, rest energy, momentum, Compton scale, and de Broglie wavelength related without conflating them?
chapters.summary: Compare leptons, nucleons, nuclei, and atomic-mass scales while keeping massive-particle rest energy E_0 = mc^2, Compton scale h/(mc), and state-dependent de Broglie wavelength h/p distinct. Linked axes show derived values rather than independent measurements, momentum is not another form of invariant mass, and composite particles require different interpretation from elementary particles.

caveats: Derived linked-axis values are not independent observations.

chapters.title: Spin, Magnetic Moments, and Anomalies
chapters.question: How does a stated spin-moment model predict magnetic response in an applied field?
chapters.summary: Calculate field-driven precession only after declaring the spin-moment model, field, state, environment, and applicable shielding or composite corrections. Keep model output separate from an identified measurement with uncertainty; measured or fitted magnetic factors do not by themselves validate a proposed geometric particle model.

caveats: A calculated response is model output, not an observation.

chapters.title: Heat, Radiation, and Bulk Matter
chapters.question: How do microscopic energy and particle counts become temperature, radiation, and laboratory-scale matter?
chapters.summary: Link Boltzmann and Avogadro scaling to ideal gases, molar quantities, black-body radiation, Wien laws, and Stefan-Boltzmann emission. Partition functions and standard-state dependence expose the assumptions and limits behind thermodynamic and bulk-matter relationships.

caveats: A chapter shell defines curriculum scope; it is not an evaluated scientific result.

chapters.title: Number Walls and Recurrence Structure
chapters.question: What can determinant patterns reveal about a sequence?
chapters.summary: Build number walls from understood recurrence sequences before examining decimal streams of constants. A visible digit pattern is not physical evidence without a preregistered statistic, a null model, and robustness under changes of units and numerical base.

caveats: A chapter shell does not report a preregistered pattern analysis.

chapters.title: Roots, Matrices, and Invariants
chapters.question: Which quantities remain fixed as polynomial roots move?
chapters.summary: Relate complex roots, Vieta identities, Newton sums, companion matrices, traces, determinants, spectral transformations, and typed units. A chosen matrix has a mathematical spectrum; that spectrum becomes physical only when a physical model derives the operator.

caveats: A mathematical spectrum is not a physical spectrum without a derived operator.

chapters.title: Discrete Rules and Continuous Fields
chapters.question: When can discrete growth rules support a continuous field model?
chapters.summary: Use substitution systems, incidence matrices, growth eigenvalues, fixed points, and density-spacing relations to compare discrete rules with continuous scalar fields. Numerical parallels such as powers of two or the golden ratio do not derive a field theory without a justified continuum limit and dynamics.

caveats: A chapter shell does not derive a continuum field theory.

chapters.title: Knots, Topology, and Soliton Stability
chapters.question: What mathematical and energetic conditions can stabilize a soliton?
chapters.summary: Distinguish knots, links, target spaces, homotopy classes, finite-energy boundaries, Derrick scaling, and stabilizing terms. Topological protection depends on the field's target space and dynamics, so topology-incompatible models and unconverged meshes cannot establish stable physical solitons.

caveats: A chapter shell does not establish a stable physical soliton.

chapters.title: From Fields to Matter
chapters.question: What must a field model derive before it can represent a particle or nucleus?
chapters.summary: Separate naming a field configuration from deriving finite-energy states, conserved charge, stability, spectra, form factors, and decay channels. Literal source formulas remain distinct from conventional calculations, and models missing operators or boundary conditions remain explicitly blocked.

caveats: Naming a field configuration does not derive a particle or nucleus.

chapters.title: Chemistry, Materials, and Thermodynamics
chapters.question: How do microscopic interactions produce chemical, material, and thermodynamic response?
chapters.summary: Study bond potentials, molecular geometry, modes, spectra, elasticity, dielectric response, interfaces, activities, phase equilibrium, equations of state, and transport. Keep source expressions separate from conventional Kramers-Kronig, Fresnel, activity, and statistical-mechanics baselines.

caveats: Source expressions and traditional baselines remain provenance-separated.

chapters.title: Planets, Stars, Galaxies, and Cosmology
chapters.question: How are gravitational models tested across planetary, stellar, galactic, and cosmological scales?
chapters.summary: Use dimensionless compactness to compare planets, stars, compact objects, and hypothetical states, then examine atmospheres, seismology, dynamos, galaxies, expansion, the cosmic microwave background, and baryon acoustic oscillations. Source claims, traditional models, survey data, selection effects, and unavailable datasets remain distinct.

caveats: A chapter shell does not report a dataset comparison.

chapters.title: Biology, Neuroscience, and Analogy
chapters.question: When does a mathematical analogy become a biological mechanism?
chapters.summary: Compare elastic rods, topological descriptions, toy kinks, cable and action-potential models, state graphs, connectome modes, and spectral inference while separating analogy from mechanism. The chapter makes no diagnostic, treatment, or consciousness claims and preserves privacy and controlled-data boundaries.

caveats: Analogy does not establish mechanism; no diagnosis, treatment, or consciousness claim is made.

chapters.title: Blind-Test Capstone
chapters.question: How can a model face a fair test without learning the answer in advance?
chapters.summary: Define the operator or action, dimensions, boundary conditions, free parameters, calibration data, frozen mapping, held-out observable, null family, uncertainty, provenance, comparison rule, and failure handling before evaluation. Apply one evidential standard across source families without asserting that their theories are equivalent.

caveats: The capstone specifies a future protocol and does not report a completed validation.
